Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (ideological framing retained)

Core mission
- Leave the EU to restore three freedoms: action (sovereign decision-making), resources (keep UK money and cut EU red tape), and people (end rule by unelected EU bodies). Replace the LibLabCon consensus with direct democracy, binding referenda, and real local control.

Economy and tax
- Turbocharge enterprise by simplifying tax: raise the personal allowance to £11,500, merge income tax and Employees’ NI into a single 31% flat rate, and phase out Employers’ NI over five years. Abolish Inheritance Tax when conditions allow.
- Cut the state back to its 1997 size, scrap quangos, and replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax that funds councils; return 50% of business rates to local authorities.
- Repeal up to 120,000 EU rules stifling business; defend the City from harmful EU directives; repatriate financial regulation.
- Restore Bank of England authority, raise bank capital ratios, split retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall style), and reinstate a “corset” on excessive lending.

Jobs, industry, and skills
- Create one million skilled jobs via long-term national programmes: defence, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport, and prison building—anchoring UK manufacturing.
- Production Enterprise Centres to help SMEs innovate and export.
- Denationalise universities/FE via universal Student/Training Vouchers; scrap EU carbon caps and protect strategic UK firms from predatory takeovers.

Immigration and asylum
- Immediate five-year freeze on permanent immigration; thereafter cap at around 50,000 per year. Leave the EU to regain border control; use time-limited work permits and visas; criminalise overstaying; triple border staff; record all entry/exit.
- No amnesty for illegal immigrants; enforce removals. Reinstate the Primary Purpose Rule; end official multiculturalism; require loyalty undertakings for residents; replace the Human Rights Act and leave the ECHR; tighten asylum with secure centres and first-safe-country rules.

Law, order, and defence
- Victims first: elected Police Boards; “life means life”; double prison places; three-strikes policy; stronger homeowner rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; youth “boot camps.”
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand the Army and TA; restore the Navy (including three carriers); strengthen the RAF; back NATO, not EU missions; maintain and renew Trident; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

Public services
- NHS: no frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; scrap wasteful tiers; franchise services on fixed budgets; Health Credit Vouchers to enable opting out; restore matrons; free eye tests and dental checks.
- Schools: universal School Vouchers; restore rigour in the three Rs; retain/expand grammar and professional schools; end social engineering; more on-the-job teacher training; elected Education Boards; allow meaningful discipline; support special schools and home education.
- Welfare: replace 70+ benefits with a flat-rate Basic Cash Benefit; allow work up to the personal allowance without penalty; enhance Child Benefit (first three children) and introduce Nursery Vouchers; limit benefits to citizens/residents of 5+ years; “Workfare” for claimants.
- Pensions: non-means-tested £130/week Citizen’s Pension at 65; retarget tax relief; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unaffordable public sector schemes; scrap PPF/NEST; avoid an EU pensions trap.

Trade, energy, and environment
- Leave the political EU; pursue a Swiss-style trade deal; reclaim the UK’s WTO seat; lead a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; seek deals with NAFTA/ASEAN; promote real human rights.
- Climate realism: repeal the Climate Change Act; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; use indigenous coal; oppose uneconomic wind (keep large schemes offshore, market-funded); exit EU carbon schemes; convene a Royal Commission on climate science; fund practical environmental improvements and flood defences; electrify transport.

Infrastructure, housing, constitution, culture
- Transport: invest £3bn/year; build high-speed rail lines; reopen railways; improve roads; fair fuel duty; “Britdisc” for foreign HGVs; oppose Heathrow expansion; build a Thames Estuary hub.
- Housing/planning: tackle demand by controlling immigration; bring empty homes into use; scrap regional quangos/IPC; binding local referenda on major schemes; protect Green Belt via elected Conservators.
- Constitution: Swiss-style initiative and referendum (5% trigger); AV+ voting; elected Police/Health/Education Boards; English-only days at Westminster, with devolved business handled by national MPs; recall powers; abolish regional government; support the monarchy and Church of England.
- Britishness: civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism/political correctness; protect iconic brands/measures; teach Britain’s contributions; counter extremist Islam (ban burqa/niqab in public buildings, deport radical preachers, reaffirm UK law over sharia); celebrate the Commonwealth; English Parliament; St George’s Day holiday.

Farming, fishing, and community
- Leave the CAP but phase support; promote British produce, ethical labelling, co-ops, and a supermarket ombudsman; review/repeal harmful EU directives.
- Exit the CFP; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end discards and industrial fishing; rebuild stocks and fleets—returning £2.5bn/year to the UK.
- Protect animal welfare; safeguard Royal Mail/Post Offices; allow designated pub smoking rooms; champion small business.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a post‑crisis programme for a future fair for all, built on active, reforming government. In the wake of the financial crash, Afghanistan and the expenses scandal, it rejects “business as usual,” pledging to secure the recovery, renew society, and restore trust in politics.

Economic strategy and fairness
- Secure the recovery by avoiding premature cuts, then more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair taxes and lower‑priority savings while protecting frontline spending on the NHS, schools, childcare and policing. Tough choices include public pay restraint, pension reform, efficiency savings and asset sales; tax fairness includes a 50p rate over £150k, a bank bonus tax, and a 1p NI rise while protecting the lowest paid.
- Reform finance to serve the real economy: tighter bank capital and pay rules, living wills, lending targets, more competition and a global levy; realise public stakes responsibly.
- Build a high‑tech, greener economy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, HS2, universal broadband, ring‑fenced science, R&D incentives, patent box, and corporate governance reform (two‑thirds takeover threshold). Create one million skilled jobs, a regional growth fund, stronger SME support and apprenticeships.

Work, welfare and living standards
- End long‑term unemployment with guarantees: jobs or training for young people after six months; mandatory job offers after two years; extend tough‑but‑fair work capability tests with support for disabled people. Minimum Wage to rise with earnings; a £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; Skills Accounts; clampdown on rogue employers.
- Help with housing and finance: stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% on £1m+ homes), more affordable homes, stronger repossession protections, a People’s Bank at the Post Office, universal access to basic bank accounts, and action on high‑cost credit.

Education and children
- Increase frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places. A legally backed 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one tuition for pupils falling behind; personal tutors in secondary; stronger leadership through accredited school groups, academies and co‑ops; parental power to trigger leadership change. Raise participation to 18, expand advanced apprenticeships and widen HE access.

NHS and care
- Protect NHS budgets, reinvest up to £20bn efficiencies, and shift to prevention and personalisation. Legal guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; mid‑life health checks; choice of qualified providers; extended GP access; talking therapies; one‑to‑one cancer nursing; more care at home.
- Create a National Care Service: free home care for the greatest needs from 2011, a cap on residential costs after two years, national standards, and expanded individual budgets. Support families with a Father’s Month, a Toddler Tax Credit, extended flexible working and an end to default retirement at 65. Re‑link the Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012 and auto‑enrol millions into pensions.

Safety, communities, immigration and culture
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood teams visible and accountable; faster action on anti‑social behaviour with a right to injunctions; expand Community Payback; use CCTV and DNA to tackle serious crime. Control immigration through the points‑based system, earned citizenship and English proficiency, aligning flows with economic need.
- Back thriving communities: protect post offices and pubs; empower supporters’ trusts in football; uphold BBC independence; deliver a golden Olympic legacy; support arts and free museums.

Green transition
- About 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 via renewables, new nuclear and clean coal/CCS; 400,000 green jobs; “pay as you save” home upgrades, smart meters, warmer homes for pensioners; move towards zero waste; protect and connect habitats, maintain the Green Belt and expand woodlands; a Supermarket Ombudsman for fair food chains.

Democratic renewal and global role
- Clean up politics and empower citizens: AV referendum, staged election of a reformed second chamber, fixed‑term parliaments, a lobbyists’ register, recall for misconduct, open data and stronger local government through Total Place.
- Support troops and veterans; a Strategic Defence Review; maintain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Lead in a reformed EU, legislate 0.7% aid from 2013, and advance climate, security and development goals.

Contrasting a pessimistic, backward‑looking Conservatism, Labour offers an optimistic, practical, progressive programme to secure recovery and build a fairer, stronger Britain.
